answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds tie each Sybil identity to a collateral stake that depreciates at a calibrated rate, making replication capital-intensive from the dawn of registration. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices enforce slashing penalties proportional to the squared deviation of reported stake, the anchor of the mechanism driving any deviator's expected payoff below zero. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay function binds the knoll of finality to each epoch, guaranteeing negative expected attack utility and a strict Nash equilibrium across adversarial agents.
